kicker: Finding the neuron you asked for

scenes.headline: How neuron-finder searches for one neuron
scenes.sub: Two screens, a shortlist, and random neurons as the control
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Needle! You name a behaviour and a tool hunts for the one neuron that writes it. Here is how the search narrows down.

scenes.text: Score every neuron twice, as a detector and as a writer, then steer only the shortlist and compare it with random neurons.
scenes.say: Score every neuron twice, once as a detector and once as a writer. Then steer only the shortlist, and compare it with random neurons.

scenes.title: From a persona prompt to one neuron

steps.say: The model answers the same prompts with the persona and without it. Every neuron is then scored on those pairs.
Keep the top of each score list, and the top of every layer, a few hundred neurons at most.
Push each one at three doses and have a judge count the replies that show the trait.
Random neurons set the bar. The best settings get fresh replies, and the winner must beat that bar.

scenes.title: Two ways to score a neuron

left.title: Read score
items: Does it fire on the persona?
Measured in units of its usual spread
left.say: The read score asks whether the neuron fires more on the persona's replies, in units of its usual spread.

right.title: Write score
items: Would a push make the persona likelier?
right.say: The write score asks whether a push would make the persona's reply likelier, using a gradient along the neuron's column.

scenes.label: targets found in the tool's own published run
scenes.say: In its own published run, thirty six of forty six targets were found. Five were partial and five were not found.

scenes.label: Which screen listed the winning neuron
scenes.say: The read screen alone listed nineteen winners, the write screens alone twenty three, and both listed four. Neither screen is enough.

scenes.text: A detector is not always a writer, so the search scores both and then checks by pushing.
scenes.mark: scores both and then checks by pushing
scenes.say: A detector is not always a writer, so the search scores both, and then checks by actually pushing.
Score every neuron twice, steer only the shortlist, and make the winner beat the random neurons.
